# Codex Product Requirements Quality Checklist: Codex Explicit Dev Flow

**Purpose**: PR-review checklist for the clarity, completeness, consistency, and measurability of the Codex product requirements, with emphasis on (A) registration/removal ownership safety and (B) thin-adapter authority, recovery, and evidence boundaries.
**Created**: 2026-08-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Depth**: Standard
**Audience / Timing**: PR reviewer before `$speckit-implement`

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are artifact identity, self-contained runtime, private/local packaging, and deferred publication requirements all specified without leaving an implied second delivery path? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001–FR-003, Scope Boundaries]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the explicit setup preconditions, supported mutations, readback, idempotent repeat, partial-failure cleanup, and conflict behavior all documented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004–FR-006, Contract §Explicit setup contract]
- [ ] CHK003 Are removal ownership, interruption recovery, repeated removal, adjacent-file preservation, npm-package separation, and retained-data behavior all documented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, User Story 3, Contract §Explicit removal contract]
- [ ] CHK004 Are every production resource and executable entry point bounded to one package, one plugin, one Skill, one MCP server, and one packaged Core runtime? [Completeness, Spec §In Scope, Plan §Project Structure]
- [ ] CHK005 Are default and explicitly overridden Core data locations separated from the registration receipt and removal ownership? [Completeness, Data Model §Registration Receipt]
- [ ] CHK006 Are package/plugin/Core version identities and receipt resource digests separated clearly from the final tarball digest recorded by the journey? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005/FR-028, Data Model §Codex Product Artifact]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is “explicit `$dev-flow` invocation” defined as an observable current-turn precondition rather than only a Skill-description preference? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010–FR-011, Contract §Invocation contract]
- [ ] CHK008 Is a substantive new requirement distinguished clearly from an explicit resume request and conversational/empty text? [Clarity, Spec §US1 scenario 3, Contract §Invocation contract]
- [ ] CHK009 Is “compatible Core Contract” measurable through named server-info properties and the exact six-tool catalog without inventing a second contract-version field? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013–FR-014, Contract §Compatibility handshake]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the supported Codex range separated clearly from the exact tested patch and unsupported host/platform evidence? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008/SC-008, Research §Decision 2]
- [ ] CHK011 Is “directly to packaged Go Core” distinguished from prohibited Node protocol/result projection while still permitting bounded lifecycle/stdio launch glue? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002/FR-016, Plan §Product boundary]
- [ ] CHK012 Is “committed workflow action” unambiguously Core state commitment rather than a Git commit performed by the adapter? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-004, Quickstart §7]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK013 Do setup requirements remain consistent across FR-003–FR-006, the plugin contract, receipt ownership model, and no-target-repository boundary? [Consistency, Spec §Product Package and Setup, Contract §Explicit setup contract]
- [ ] CHK014 Do removal requirements consistently preserve Core data while allowing only recorded Codex registration and receipt cleanup? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007/US3/SC-007, Data Model §Identity and ownership]
- [ ] CHK015 Do Skill requirements and the governed loop consistently leave action selection, payload schemas, recovery advice, and terminal outcomes to Core? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015–FR-024, Contract §Governed action loop]
- [ ] CHK016 Does the selected plugin/marketplace design remain consistent with the no-manual-global-config success criterion and explicit user setup requirement? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004/SC-001, Contract §Reconciliation sequence]
- [ ] CHK017 Are the shared fixture count/digest, Core Contract 0.1 reference, and exact tool names consistent across plan, research, contracts, and evidence schema? [Consistency, Plan §Phase 0, Research §Decision 1]
- [ ] CHK018 Are private local packaging and final-artifact evidence requirements consistent with the explicit exclusion of public npm/GitHub publication? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001/FR-027, Out of Scope]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK019 Are primary install, explicit new-task, restart/resume, completion, removal, and compatible reinstall scenarios each described independently? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories 1–3]
- [ ] CHK020 Are alternate paths for already-registered setup, already-removed product, an exact compatible active task, and a subdirectory/symlink worktree specified? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Contract §Reconciliation sequence]
- [ ] CHK021 Are exception requirements defined for incompatible Codex, missing/non-executable runtime, malformed host readback, non-Git input, multi-repository scope, and ownership conflict? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases/FR-005/FR-012/FR-020]
- [ ] CHK022 Are recovery requirements complete for lost/truncated mutation responses, interrupted setup, interrupted removal, and stale plugin registry visibility? [Coverage, Spec §US2 scenario 3/Edge Cases, Contracts §Recovery-before-retry and Explicit removal]
- [ ] CHK023 Is concurrency behavior bounded by Core's unique compatible task/claim result rather than an adapter-side session-selection rule? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020 and Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 Are unavailable-by-policy and unsupported-surface cases required to produce explicit blocked/failed evidence rather than an unsupported success claim? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases/FR-028/SC-008, Evidence Schema]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK025 Can one reviewer objectively determine that setup registered exactly one Skill/server and left the target repository untouched? [Measurability, Spec §US1 scenarios 1/4, SC-001]
- [ ] CHK026 Can explicit-only behavior be measured as zero calls to the six Dev Flow tools and zero tasks for an ordinary prompt, distinct from host transport discovery, plus a pre-open stop for invalid explicit input? [Measurability, Spec §US1 scenarios 2/3, SC-002]
- [ ] CHK027 Can new-versus-resumed behavior be measured through one opaque task ID and continuing revisions without adapter-owned task state? [Measurability, Spec §US2 scenarios 1/2, SC-003/SC-004]
- [ ] CHK028 Can read-before-retry be established from an ordered call trace that retains the original mutation identity and uses a fresh Core assessment? [Measurability, Spec §FR-022/FR-026, Contract §Recovery-before-retry]
- [ ] CHK029 Can verification-budget compliance be measured from exact automatic-command counts and distinct manual/simulated/native evidence labels? [Measurability, Spec §FR-023/SC-005, Contract §Evidence and verification budget]
- [ ] CHK030 Can safe removal be measured through plugin/marketplace readback, receipt absence, equal data digests, task reopen, and repository fingerprint comparison? [Measurability, Spec §US3/SC-007, Evidence Schema]

## Edge Cases and Non-Functional Boundaries

- [ ] CHK031 Are stdout purity, spaces/Unicode/symlink paths, role-policy availability, and truncated-result edge cases tied to explicit fail-closed requirements? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, Contracts §Product executable/Presentation]
- [ ] CHK032 Is the absence of a new throughput/latency target intentional and consistent with a single inherited-stdio process and no polling/proxy requirement? [Non-Functional, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK033 Are security/ownership requirements sufficient to prevent symlink escape, shell interpolation, direct config/cache deletion, recursive cleanup, and secret capture in evidence? [Coverage, Contract §Setup Preconditions/Error and evidence rules]
- [ ] CHK034 Are platform and compatibility failures required to happen before registration mutation and without a runtime fallback? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-002/FR-005/SC-008, Contract §Setup Preconditions]

## Dependencies, Assumptions, and Scope

- [ ] CHK035 Is Feature 002 delivery, Core Contract 0.1, and the 22-file shared fixture baseline documented as a validated dependency rather than future work? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions, Research §Decision 1]
- [ ] CHK036 Are OpenAI documentation access date, official-source links, selected CLI range, and the local 0.146.0 evidence limitation explicit enough for later revalidation? [Dependency, Spec §FR-008, Research §Decision 2/Official source index]
- [ ] CHK037 Are publication, automatic update, multi-platform selection, other Codex surfaces, DeepSeek behavior, Git management, and cross-host takeover explicitly excluded from Feature 003? [Scope, Spec §Out of Scope, Plan §Delivery Boundary]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the minimal internal Core version seam justified without implying a Core contract, state, schema, or release-framework change? [Assumption, Plan §Complexity Tracking, Research §Decision 6]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add reviewer findings inline and link them to the affected specification or planning artifact.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
